t: Minimum Number of Lines to Cover Points — Bitmask DP Over Collinear Sets
o: Any two points define a line, and an optimal covering bundles collinear points together: in example 1 the diagonal swallows (0,1), (2,3), (4,5) while a horizontal covers (2,3), (4,3), for 2 lines total; example 2's three points are collinear, needing just 1. Because any line covers at least two points, the answer never exceeds ⌈n/2⌉, and with n ≤ 10 exhaustive search over subsets is entirely viable. Precomputing, for each pair, the bitmask of all points collinear with it (cross product equal to zero) turns coverage into set algebra: anchor every new line at the lowest-indexed uncovered point, cover everything on that line, and recurse on what remains.
k: Point k lies on the line through i and j iff (x_j − x_i)(y_k − y_i) == (y_j − y_i)(x_k − x_i) — slope comparison without division or floats.
Anchoring each new line at the lowest uncovered point removes permutation symmetry between equivalent orderings.
Line masks make coverage O(1) bit work, and n ≤ 10 keeps the state space at ≤ 1024 subsets.

a.i: Pick the lowest-indexed uncovered point i and try a line through i and every other uncovered point j (with j = i covering i alone), removing all newly covered points each time. This explores overlapping subproblems repeatedly and is exponential, but acceptable because n ≤ 10.
s: Precompute line[i][j] = bitmask of all points on the line through points i and j, defining line[i][i] = {i}.
Recursive go(mask): return 0 when mask is empty.
Anchor i at the lowest set bit of mask.
For every uncovered j, recurse on mask minus line[i][j] and take the smallest 1 + result.
a.t: Exponential (≈ n!! recursion tree) — overlapping subsets are recomputed; fine only because n ≤ 10.

a.i: Define dp[mask] = fewest lines covering exactly the subset mask. Every chosen line contains the anchor point i (the lowest set bit), so transitions strictly shrink the mask; one ascending sweep therefore finalizes each dp[mask] from already-computed strictly smaller states.
s: Build line[][] via cross-product collinearity, special-casing i == j as the singleton mask.
Set dp[0] = 0 and iterate mask from 1 to 2ⁿ − 1 ascending.
With anchor i = lowest set bit, compute dp[mask] = 1 + min(dp[mask & ~line[i][j]]) over set bits j.
a.t: O(2ⁿ · n + n³) — cubic preprocessing of line masks, then each of 2ⁿ masks tries at most n partners.

w: Anchor every line at the lowest uncovered point — trying arbitrary pairs wastes a factorial factor on symmetric orders. The i == j degenerate pair is the classic bug: its zero direction vector makes every point test 'collinear' unless special-cased as a singleton. Cross products beat floating-point slopes on both precision and speed. Follow-ups: reconstruct which lines were used, handle duplicate points (they merge into one), or scale beyond tiny n with exact-cover-style branch-and-bound.
